provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Rice husk phytolith (biogenic silica microstructure) as bio-adsorbent.

mechanisms.description: Rice husk silica surface adsorption: silanol groups (Si-OH) on rice husk-derived silica provide binding sites for heavy metals via complexation and ion exchange

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions and organic pollutants

interaction.text: Complexation and ion exchange with silanol groups
interaction.quote: Rice-straw biochar with high silica content shows a greater adsorption capacity for Cd over pure biochar.

why_it_works.text: Enhanced adsorption with high silica content rice husk biochar
why_it_works.scope_match: Keywords: adsorption, biochar, content, en, high
why_it_works.quote: Rice-straw biochar with high silica content shows a greater adsorption capacity for Cd over pure biochar.

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Rice husk phytolith biogenic silica microstructure provides high surface area for adsorption

mechanisms.verification_quote: Rice-straw biochar with high silica content shows a greater adsorption capacity for Cd over pure biochar.

engineering_constraints.description: Rice husk silica extraction: combustion at 500-700°C or acid leaching followed by calcination

narrative.text: Rice husks contain 15-20% silica by weight, making them an abundant source of biosilica. The silica exists in amorphous form and can be extracted via simple combustion, creating high-surface-area adsorbent material.

design_translation.idea: Extract silica from rice husk agricultural waste via combustion or acid treatment, use as adsorbent for heavy metals and organic pollutants
examples: Rice husk biochar with high silica for Cd adsorption
Rice husk silica nanoparticles for pollutant removal
design_translation.applicability: Heavy metal removal from wastewater; low-cost adsorbent from agricultural waste
